packs.title: Water Rooms and Sky Lines
packs.promise: Find Milan beyond the centre in canal connections, green levels and three different ways to meet the sky.

q.s: Let a broad water basin make room for one unhurried thought.
st: Choose one long boundary where the water meets its bank, using the official image if the approach is uncomfortable. Settle somewhere stopped with your return route in mind.
Let your attention follow that boundary for as long as feels comfortable. Notice where you would choose to stop looking; there is no need to trace the whole basin or follow passing people.
Save one short sentence beginning with your own choice of pace word, then describe the part of the bank where you let your attention settle.

q.s: Borrow a row of columns for a small structure of your own.
st: Choose a column shaft, its wider top and the horizontal line above the row. Describe one difference between these three visible parts.

Design an imaginary folded-paper stand for a lightweight object of your choice. Borrow a vertical support, a widening joint and a horizontal resting line from the columns; draw the stand or describe it in words.
Save your design with its three borrowed parts and the object it would hold. No real construction, engineering test or alteration to the monument is required.

q.s: Collect three height relationships in an outdoor artwork.
st: Find three egg-topped poles at different apparent heights in the artwork or its official photograph. Compare from one stopped viewpoint; no circling or measuring is needed.
Describe two relationships among your three choices, such as higher than, close beside or separated from. Use height and position rather than color if you prefer.
Save your three choices and two relationships. Arrange three dots on paper or in a written line to represent that small part of the artwork, leaving the real work untouched.

packs.title: Small Signals, Big City
packs.promise: Find a story in the details between Milan’s grand façades and green paths.

q.s: Collect three moods from one pale façade.
st: Stop in a roomy public place where you can see part of the Duomo’s marble exterior without joining an entrance queue.
Find three patches that look different: one bright, one shaded and one with a visible change of tone. If the light is even, choose three differences in texture or colour instead.
Give each patch a one-word mood based on what you see. Arrange your three words from the quietest mood to the liveliest.
Save the three observed patches and your ordered words.

q.s: Follow light across three different surfaces.
st: Choose a comfortable stopping place along an open side of the covered passage. Look upward only as far as feels easy.
Find glass, a metal roof line and a solid wall surface. Notice whether each lets light through, makes a dark outline or holds a patch of brightness.
Pair each surface with one of those effects. Find a place where two of your surfaces meet and describe the join.
Save your three surface-and-light pairs and the join.

q.t: A Book Jacket for a Lane
q.s: Turn three street details into an imaginary book.
st: From a comfortable place on Via Fiori Chiari, choose three visible details: a doorway shape, a window feature and a paving pattern.
Imagine those details belong on the cover of a book. Sketch their arrangement or describe where each would sit on the cover.
Give the imaginary book an original three-word title. Add one sentence about the adventure a reader might find inside.
Save your cover arrangement, title and sentence.
